cases.name: Poseidon Wave Media LLC v. Suno, Inc.
UMG Recordings, Sony Music et al. v. Suno, Inc.

profile_text.body:
Suno describes itself as an AI music generator that creates complete original songs, including vocals, lyrics, and production, from a single text prompt in under a minute. The company says users can describe a genre, mood, or theme, or provide their own lyrics, and then regenerate, extend, or refine the track. Suno also presents Suno Studio as a web-based generative audio workstation that combines traditional DAW functionality with AI-powered music creation. The company states the service is free forever, with paid plans adding features such as 500 songs a month on Pro and 2,000 songs a month on Premier, access to the v5.5 model, stem separation, MIDI export, Persona Voices, and audio uploads of up to 8 minutes.

Suno is a for-profit startup founded in 2022 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Its product, Suno, is categorized under voice and audio and is described as a music generation tool. The company positions the product as a beat maker, AI song generator, and song creator in one, and says millions of people use it for fun, content, and professional projects.

Court records list Suno Inc. as a defendant in eight federal district court cases. These include UMG Recordings, Sony Music et al. v. Suno, Inc. in the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts. Other cases name Gawronski, Rugnetta, Pilavian, Reyna, S.A. Jamendo, Poseidon Wave Media LLC, and Woulard as plaintiffs in the Southern District of Texas, District of Massachusetts, Southern District of New York, and Northern District of Illinois. Court records show 191 Massachusetts entries involving Suno.
